title: Effectiveness of Total Workplace Safety and Health Approach
what_it_is: Effectiveness of Total Workplace Safety and Health Approach

sections.label: Workplace fatalities and injuries question
sections.summary: A question asked whether workplace fatalities and injuries spiked and whether the Total WSH approach is failing, with preliminary data showing a slight rise in the non-fatal major injury rate in 2019.

sentences.text: The following question stood in the name of  Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong –  21 To ask the Minister for Manpower whether there has been a spike in workplace fatalities and injuries in the past year and whether the Total Workplace Safety and Health approach is failing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: However, preliminary data shows that the non-fatal major injury rate crept up slightly in 2019 when compared to 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: More details will be released in the 2019 National Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Statistics Report by end February 2020.

sections.label: Major injury rate improvement
sections.summary: The major injury rate improved over five years from 20 in 2014 to 17.4 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Likewise, the major injury rate has also improved over the last five years from 20 in 2014 to 17.4 in 2018.

sections.label: WSH 2028 roadmap and Total WSH
sections.summary: Singapore aims for a workplace fatal injury rate below one per 100,000 workers by 2028, with Total WSH part of the approach to reduce accidents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: As outlined in our WSH 2028 roadmap, Singapore aims to achieve and sustain a workplace fatal injury rate of less than one per 100,000 workers by 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Amongst the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) member countries, only four have achieved this level of performance on a sustained basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: One key challenge in realising this aspiration is the risk of increasing ill-health among the workforce, including chronic diseases like diabetes, high blood pressure and high cholesterol.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: To reduce accidents in a sustainable manner, we will need more attention on supporting health, not just improving safety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Total WSH is part of our comprehensive approach to prevent and reduce accidents over the longer term.
